P8F-1 finding (2026-07-24): the on-file data/rules/south-korea.json content is INCORRECT/OVERSTATED and must be corrected at P8F-2. cash_declaration_threshold says No mandatory currency declaration threshold and bring_foreign_currency_in says travellers should be prepared to declare if questioned — but Korea Customs requires a MANDATORY declaration when means of payment (foreign currency, Korean-won notes or checks) exceed USD 10,000 in total, via item no. 3 of the Traveler Declaration Form, yielding a Certificate of Foreign Currency Declaration (legal basis: Foreign Exchange Transactions Act).

P8F-1 finding: exchange_controls/overview claim (no general exchange controls; fully liberalised for both current and capital account) is OVERSTATED. Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FETA) the current account is liberalised but capital transactions with large fund movements follow separate transaction-type reporting/notification procedures (reported to the Bank of Korea Governor / MOEF / a foreign exchange bank), banks report FX sales over USD 10,000 to the National Tax Administration, and the Korean won is not fully internationalized. Remove the absolute fully liberalised wording at P8F-2 and describe the FETA notification regime.

P8F-1 finding: keep four regimes strictly separate — (a) Korea Customs USD 10,000 border currency declaration; (b) FETA capital-transaction reporting/notification to BOK/MOEF/foreign exchange banks; (c) bank reporting of FX sales over USD 10,000 to the National Tax Administration; (d) KoFIU AML/CFT reporting. South Korea sourced as its own jurisdiction.

P8F-1 note: Korea Customs pages are JS-shell for WebFetch (content confirmed via the official customs.go.kr search result and the live page returning HTTP 200); BOK Foreign Exchange System pages fetch cleanly (HTTP 200). Exact figures, form field numbers, FETA article numbers and current effective dates to be pinned at the P8F-2 publication-candidate review; FETA consolidated English text on law.go.kr; on-file source_authorities cite FSS (supervisor) — MOEF+BOK administer FETA and should be sourced explicitly.

P8F-2 outcome (2026-07-24): data/rules/south-korea.json CORRECTED. All P8F-1 defects fixed: cash_declaration_threshold now states the MANDATORY declaration for means of payment (foreign currency + KRW notes + checks) exceeding USD 10,000 in total (Korea Customs; Traveler Declaration Form item 3; Certificate of Foreign Currency Declaration; triggered only above USD 10,000); bring/take fields state the mandatory procedure (declare-if-questioned removed); the fully-liberalised and no-exchange-controls absolutes removed and replaced with the FETA three-area structure (current liberalised; capital transactions notification/permission via foreign exchange banks / BOK Governor / MOEF; won not fully internationalised). Declaration, exchange_controls, banking_conversion and overview CLOSED with official sources (Korea Customs page; BOK Foreign Exchange System guidance). Four fields remain [HARDENING] — resident_holding_rules, non_resident_rules, business_invoicing_settlement, summary.business — because the exact FETA article/enforcement-decree text is JS-gated on law.go.kr and KLRI. Per the readiness rule, South Korea is HELD at source_review_ready; no governance exception. Blocker for P8F-2b: fetch/pin the exact FETA articles for the capital account-level fields.

P8F-2b outcome (2026-07-24): all four [HARDENING] fields CLOSED on the controlling FETA text obtained via the KLRI official English reference translation (elaw.klri.re.kr eng_mobile viewer, which serves the article body where the law.go.kr/KLRI desktop shells are JS-gated). Pinpointed provisions: Foreign Exchange Transactions Act Art. 3 (definitions of resident, non-resident, capital transactions), Art. 8 (registration of foreign exchange business), Art. 15 (payment procedures; permission for certain payments abroad), Art. 16 (reporting on methods of payment or receipt — offsetting a claim; settlement outside the Minister's period; third-party payment; payment/receipt without going through a foreign exchange agency), Art. 18 (advance reporting on capital transactions), Art. 23 (delegation to the BOK Governor, FSC and foreign exchange agencies); Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulations (Notice No. 2023-26, Jul. 4, 2023) Art. 2-6-2 (resident accounts and resident FC trust accounts; external/non-resident FC trust accounts; non-resident won and non-resident free-transfer won accounts) and Art. 2-6 (declaration to the BOK Governor for specified transactions). The four separate regimes — Korea Customs USD 10,000 border declaration; FETA capital-transaction/method-of-payment reporting; bank reporting of FX sales over USD 10,000 to the National Tax Service; KoFIU AML/CFT — remain distinct; no invoice-currency choice asserted (the Act does not govern it); no account/service entitlement implied. Zero [HARDENING] markers remain. All five governance gates pass. South Korea advanced source_review_ready -> publish_ready. Not published, not indexed, no public surface.
